title: Platform systems & services: how-tos, dashboards, alerts, runbooks, retrospectives, and roadmap (Q1 2028)
author: Marco Chen
summary: This living doc consolidates platform systems and services guidance: how-tos for common platform tasks, dashboard and alert standards, operational runbooks for high-priority incidents, recent retrospectives with tracked action items, and the Q1 2028 roadmap. It is the canonical team wiki entry for platform oncall and engineering partners.
overview: Purpose: give platform engineers and adjacent teams a single reference for operating Redwood's platform systems (control plane, ingress, routing, telemetry, autoscaler, GPU scheduler) with reproducible procedures and observable standards. Use this doc for onboarding, incident response, runbook maintenance, and planning. Scope: hosted control plane, Dedicated control loops, observability stack (Prometheus/Thanos, Grafana, Loki), alert-routing (PagerDuty/Slack), primary services (route-traffic, model-router, kv-cache, batching-service, autoscaler).
systems_and_services:
Core services and short ownership:
- route-traffic: ownership eng-platform/networking; responsibility: global routing, region failover, TLS termination.
- model-router: ownership eng-serving-runtime; responsibility: variant routing, fallback policies.
- kv-cache: ownership eng-serving-runtime; responsibility: prefix caching, cache invalidation API.
- batching-service: ownership eng-platform/batching; responsibility: request coalescing, batch sizing policy.
- autoscaler: ownership eng-sre; responsibility: scaling pools for Dedicated and hosted pools.
- telemetry-stack (prometheus/thanos/grafana/loki): ownership eng-platform/observability; responsibility: metrics collection, retention, dashboards, and alerting.

howtos:
Common how-tos (follow the steps exactly and update runbook after changes):
1) Add a Grafana dashboard for a service:
   - Copy templates/dashboard-template.json to /dashboards/<service>-overview.json
   - Update variables: service_name, prometheus_datasource, alert_tags
   - Commit to infra/dashboards repo and open PR with screenshots
   - On merge, CI will import dashboard to Grafana using grafana-cli
2) Create an alert rule (Prometheus):
   - Add rule to prometheus/rules/<team>/<service>-alerts.yaml
   - Use alert naming convention: PLAT_<SERVICE>_<SHORT_DESCRIPTION>
   - Include severity (sev1|sev2|sev3), runbook_url, owner_team label
   - Validate with promtool check rules and run CI lint
   - Deploy via k8s/helm chart and confirm firing in staging
3) Deploy a config change to model-router:
   - Branch from main, bump image tag, update configmap with rollout policy
   - Canary: deploy to canary namespace 2 pods for 30m, run acceptance tests (latency/quality)
   - If green, promote using rolling update to production 5%->20%->100% over 40m windows
   - On regression, rollback to previous tag and notify #model-serving
dashboards_and_alerts:
Standards and examples:
- Dashboard convention: Overview (SLOs & errors) -> Performance (latency P50/P95/P99) -> Throughput & utilization -> Cost signals (GPU hours, token/sec) -> Recent incidents/events panel.
- Metric naming: use service_prefix_metric (e.g., model_router_request_latency_seconds_bucket). Add 'team' and 'service' labels for filtering.
- SLOs (examples):
  - control-plane-api: availability SLO 99.95% monthly, error_budget 0.05%.
  - inference-path latency: P95 < 120ms for cached requests, P95 < 400ms for cold model loads.
- Alert thresholds (examples):
  - HighErrorRate (sev1): rate(http_requests_total{job="control-plane",code=~"5.."}[5m]) > 0.01 for 10m -> PagerDuty P1
    Example PromQL: sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="control-plane",code=~"5.."}[5m])) by (service) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{job="control-plane"}[5m])) by (service) > 0.01
  - HighHostCPU (sev2): avg(node_cpu_seconds_total{mode!="idle"}[5m]) by (instance) > 0.85 -> Alert to #platform-ops
  - QueueDepthGrowth (sev1): increase(batching_queue_length[2m]) > 100 -> PagerDuty P1
- Alert routing: PagerDuty for sev1, Slack + ticket for sev2, Slack-only for sev3. Use alert annotations: runbook, playbook_link, paging_hours.
- Dashboard ownership: every dashboard must list owner and last_reviewed date in the dashboard description.
runbooks:
Primary runbooks (abbreviated) — full runbooks should live in /runbooks repo and link here:
1) control-plane-high-error-rate (sev1):
   - Symptoms: 5xx rate > 1% for >10m, errors correlated to a specific service.
   - Immediate actions:
     1. Acknowledge PagerDuty, create incident in JIRA (INC-<ts>).
     2. Check grafana dashboards: control-plane overview, recent deploys, error logs in Loki.
     3. If a recent deploy exists, rollback via helm rollback <release> to previous revision.
     4. If no deploy, scale down traffic to affected region: kubectl patch svc --patch '{"spec":{"trafficPolicy":...}}' OR use route-traffic API to divert.
     5. If memory OOMs, cordon and drain node: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets <node>.
   - Post-incident: run retrospective template and assign action items.
2) inference-latency-degradation (sev1/sev2):
   - Symptoms: P95 latency jump + increased queue depth.
   - Mitigations:
     - Enable autoscaler burst policy: autoscaler api set-burst --pool <pool> --factor 2
     - Temporarily enable prefix caching for heavy routes: kv-cache admin enable-prefix <prefix>
     - Reduce batch window size: update batching-service config batch_max_wait_ms to 5ms and roll.
   - Escalation: If mitigations fail in 20m, page eng-sre and model-serving leads.
3) disk-pressure-on-observability (sev2):
   - Symptoms: Thanos compactor backlog > 6h, alerts for low-disk.
   - Steps: increase retention throttling, rotate older blocks to cold storage, increase PVC size (k8s patch) and restart compactor.
Commands and examples included inline where applicable. Always update the runbook 'last_reviewed' field after an incident.
retrospective:
Recent retrospectives (summary and action items):
- Incident: control-plane partial outage on 2027-11-22 (INC-20271122-1)
  - Root cause: cascading autoscaler misconfiguration and a canary that increased steady-state resource pressure.
  - Actions:
    - (Owner: Priya Singh) Add autoscaler safety caps and circuit-breaker thresholds by 2028-01-15 — DONE
    - (Owner: Marco Chen) Add pre-deploy resource pressure test to CI by 2028-02-01 — IN_PROGRESS
    - (Owner: Aisha Patel) Create synthetic traffic job for canary validation by 2028-01-10 — DONE
- Incident: high model-router error rate on 2028-01-05 (INC-20280105-3)
  - Root cause: regression in retry middleware exposing a downstream NPE.
  - Actions:
    - (Owner: Diego Rivera) Add unit and integration tests around retry middleware by 2028-02-10 — DONE
    - (Owner: Lena Thompson) Add canary health-check step to block deploys with elevated latency by 2028-02-20 — IN_PROGRESS
Retrospective cadence: after every sev1 we schedule a blameless postmortem within 7 days and track actions in the platform backlog.
roadmap:
Quarterly roadmap (near-term priorities):

  - Implement dynamic batching tuning service (Owner: Lena Thompson)

  - Observability retention policy v2: reduce hot retention from 30d to 14d for infra metrics (Owner: Platform Observability)
- Q2 2028:
  - Private deployment observability bundle (onprem-friendly) (Owner: Eng Private Deployments)
  - Traffic-shaping policy engine (Owner: Marco Chen)
Roadmap notes: each item must have a spec doc, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan. Link specs in references section.
ownership_and_oncall:
Oncall and ownership:
- Primary oncall: eng-platform oncall rotation (2-week rotations). Escalation: primary -> secondary -> eng-sre lead.
- PagerDuty: policy 'platform-prod' for sev1 pages; contact triangle includes primary, service owner, eng-sre.
- Slack channels: #platform-oncall (pages and urgent comms), #platform-retros (postmortem threads), #platform-deploys (deploy chatter).
- Runbook maintenance: each service owner must review their runbooks and dashboards at least quarterly and mark 'last_reviewed' in the dashboard description.
- Handover: on rotation change, outgoing oncall publishes a 30-minute async handover message in #platform-oncall with ongoing incidents, mitigations, and outstanding actions.
